## The question

Can workplaces support circadian health for people with different schedules and needs? Access to daylight, opportunities for breaks and control over work timing may be unevenly distributed.

## The project

Investigate circadian accessibility as a question of both environment and organisation. A focused project could assess workplace guidance, examine a defined setting or explore experiences through interviews. The aim is to identify constraints and practical opportunities without assuming one schedule suits everyone.

## What you will do

- Connect evidence about light and daily timing with workplace design and occupational health.
- Develop a bounded assessment, document study or interview approach, with approvals where needed.
- Analyse environmental or organisational barriers and communicate findings with their limitations.

## Possible scope

A thesis could combine an evidence review with an empirical case study. A shorter placement could map guidance or one aspect of workplace access. Architecture, occupational health and social research perspectives are especially welcome.
